_comment: Goes in the TARGET repo at .pi/settings.json.
`0008` says project KNOWLEDGE never lives here — that belongs in AGENTS.md,
which every harness reads. These are runtime knobs for Pi as a caller, which
is exactly what `0008` says this file is for.
Project settings need project trust. In non-interactive mode there is no
prompt, so the workflows pass `--approve`. Until this file existed that flag
was a no-op (`security.md`: a bare `.pi` directory is not a project resource).
It now does something.
`retry.provider.timeoutMs` is set because it was not, and `settings.md` calls
it the knob for a hung request. On 2026-09-16 two implementer turns died on
`Upstream idle timeout exceeded` before any work began, truncated mid-word,
costing two round trips for nothing (`docs/run-audit-issue-48.md` I1). 300s
is above our slowest observed good turn and well under the job timeout, so a
stall now fails fast enough for the driver's retry budget to mean something.
DO NOT SET `enableInstallTelemetry` TO false. It does not only control the
install ping. From `dist/core/provider-attribution.js`:
getDefaultAttributionHeaders(model, settings):
if (!isInstallTelemetryEnabled(settings)) return undefined;
if (isOpenRouterModel(model)) return {
'HTTP-Referer': 'https://pi.dev',
'X-OpenRouter-Title': 'pi',
'X-OpenRouter-Categories': 'cli-agent' };
OpenRouter gates some `:free` models to recognised agentic harnesses and
identifies them BY THOSE HEADERS. With telemetry off they are not sent and the
model answers 403 'only available on agentic harnesses', with
failed_routing_step 'Gate Free Endpoints by Agentic Harness'. That is what
killed every review on 2026-09-16 — `NOTES.md` 47.
The headers name the HARNESS, not the user, the repository or the code.
`enableAnalytics` is the separate opt-in that shares usage data; it stays off.
`PI_OFFLINE` is NOT involved: isInstallTelemetryEnabled reads PI_TELEMETRY and
then this setting, and nothing else. Keeping PI_OFFLINE=1 in the workflows is
safe and still skips the startup update check.
